headline: Nvidia's chief executive said American companies should use Chinese AI models and warned against banning them, answering a US Treasury threat to sanction developers accused of theft.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 2: the same Stocktwits article ran in our 28 Sep 2026 edition and the remarks predate 11 Oct, so this is old news re-dated with no new development.
importance_line: A major chip maker's chief pushing back on a US sanctions threat bears on American firms choosing which AI to use, then on Chinese developers, then on Nvidia, which sells the chips for both; it is one executive's view, and the interview is at least two weeks old.
summary: Stocktwits reports that Jensen Huang, chief executive of the chip maker Nvidia, told Axios that American companies should "absolutely" use Chinese AI models and that the real worry is the campaign to ban them, answering Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's warning the day before that the US can sanction overseas model makers found to be stealing from American companies, which our 28 Sep 2026 edition carried from Stocktwits. Huang also said Anthropic's cyber-security model Claude Mythos, which only a limited set of US companies can use, "should be available as a service", and argued that free, open AI will raise demand for the chips and data centres that Nvidia and others sell; this is the interview we carried on 28 Sep 2026, made on a Wednesday that the article does not date.
notes: Read the Stocktwits article in full. Older news re-dated: pool date 11 Oct 2026 but the same URL ran in our 28 Sep 2026 edition as headline only; the article gives no calendar date. Reply to Bessent's Tuesday warning (our 28 Sep 2026 edition, Stocktwits, separate URL).
